title: CRITICAL: prove keyboard input reaches AVM1 in published SWFs (Key.isDown e2e)
description: Found by the 0519 capstone and sidestepped with an auto-chase workaround: no test anywhere proves that keyboard input drives game logic in our published SWFs. The closure claimed 'headless Ruffle does not reliably drive onEnterFrame with keyboard input' — asserted, never demonstrated, and suspect: Ruffle handles keyboard fine in browsers; the usual gotcha is FOCUS (the ruffle-player element must be clicked/focused before page.keyboard events reach it; also check tabindex and that the embed isn't in a cross-origin frame). Scope: minimal e2e — publish a movie whose script moves a clip with Key.isDown(Key.RIGHT) in onEnterFrame (or onClipEvent(enterFrame)); in Playwright, click the Ruffle player to focus it, hold/press ArrowRight via page.keyboard, assert the clip visibly moves (pixel diff region check). Triage Ruffle's key handling (ruffle clone: core/src/avm1 Key + desktop/web input plumbing) if focus alone doesn't fix it. This unblocks the 0519 capstone's real play-the-game acceptance. Evidence: command + pass summary pasted here.
